classification.difficultyReason: Combines similar triangles, circular area, cone volume and conservation of volume.

content.prompt:
In this question you will need to use the following formula:

Volume of a cone, $$V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h.$$

A right circular cone has height 20 cm and radius 9 cm, as shown in the diagram.

spec.description: Inverted cone; the 9 cm arrow measures the radius from the rim centre to its right edge. No water level is supplied.
spec.mathematics: Full height 20 cm; full radius 9 cm; dashed diameter and axial height meet at the rim centre.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry remains visible; no calculated water radius or level is shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Water is poured into the inverted cone until the depth of the water is 14 cm.

children.label: i
children.prompt: If $r$ centimetres is the radius of the water’s surface, use similar triangles to calculate the value of $r$.

answer.worked:
The axial cross-sections form similar triangles.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{r}{9}&=\frac{14}{20}\\r&=9\times\frac{14}{20}\\r&=6.3.\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Use your answer to calculate the area of the water’s surface, giving your answer in decimal form correct to 2 decimal places.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The cone is now filled right to the top with water. What is the volume of the water in the cone, correct to the nearest $0.1\text{ cm}^3$?

children.label: c
children.prompt:
The water is then poured from the cone into the rectangular tank shown.

Calculate the depth of water in the tank, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Perspective rectangular tank with visible edges solid and hidden edges dashed black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal base 20 cm by 15 cm; vertical height 10 cm.

answer.worked:
The volume is unchanged. Let the depth be $d$ centimetres.

$$\begin{align*}20\times15\times d&=540\pi\\d&=\frac{540\pi}{300}\\d&=1.8\pi\\d&\approx5.65\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

This is below the tank’s 10 cm height.
